docs.title: Objects and models
docs.text:
Tired of the standard-issue barrel? A mod can give the game's objects a new look: furniture, fences, guns, signs, posters, workbenches and training equipment. You either drop in your own 3D model, or keep the game's model and paint it with a new texture. You can also give an object a new icon in the build menu.

Only the look changes. Size on the grid, cost, health, where crew stand to use it, and every other rule stay as the game defines them. Changing numbers is done with CSV tables.

Example files

Ready-made example models, textures, thumbnails and export presets are in the example folder on Google Drive. Use them as a reference for how your own files should look.

Everything for objects goes into one folder in your mod, Objects/:

Mods/
  my_mod/
    Objects/
      Chair.glb               your model for the chair
      Chair.destroyed.glb     the chair when it is destroyed
      Chair.thumbnail.png     the chair's new icon in the build menu
      Chair_BaseMap_1001.png  a texture for it
      config.json             optional settings

Restart after every change

Art is imported once, when the game starts. After you add or change a model, texture or thumbnail, quit the game completely and start it again. Loading a save, Refresh and the Enabled switch in the Mods window do not re-import art.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Give the chair a new model:

  1. Build your chair in your 3D program at the size of the game's chair (in metres) and export it as Chair.glb (binary glTF) or Chair.fbx. Build its destroyed look too and export it as Chair.destroyed.glb or Chair.destroyed.fbx.
  2. Name the chair's material in your 3D program, for example MyChair, and save its colour texture as MyChair_BaseMap_1001.png.
  3. Put all three files into Mods/my_mod/Objects/.
  4. Restart the game and load a save. Every chair, the ones already standing and new ones you build, now uses your model.

Just want to recolour the game's own chair? You do not need a model at all: see Re-painting without a model.

docs.title: Which objects can be changed
docs.text:
A model's file name is the id of the object it replaces. You can change the objects you place from the build menu, including workbenches and training objects, for example Chair, FieldKitchen or ShootingSimpleTargetRange. Every object you can change is listed in our moddable objects table, together with how we built it ourselves: material naming and usage, texture resolution, UDIM information and its destroyed view.

Ids are matched without regard to capital letters, so chair.fbx changes the chair too.

Only these objects can be re-dressed with Objects/. Trees, rocks and the other things placed on a map cannot be changed by a mod yet. Airplanes get new paint schemes another way: see Airplane skins. The ground is changed with biomes.

docs.title: File names
docs.text:
Every file that belongs to one object is named <objectId>, <objectId>.destroyed or <objectId>.thumbnail, plus its extension:

File What it is Chair.fbx or Chair.glb the chair's model Chair.destroyed.fbx the model the chair switches to when it is destroyed Chair.thumbnail.png the chair's icon in the build menu
  • Models may be .glb (binary glTF) or .fbx. If both exist for the same object, the .glb is used and the .fbx is reported in the log as ignored.
  • Blender's duplicate names such as Chair.001.fbx are refused. Rename the file before you copy it in.
  • A destroyed model is required. The game always shows an object's destroyed look, so every model you ship needs a .destroyed model next to it. The moddable objects table shows the destroyed view of each object.
  • Anything else in the folder that is not a model, a PNG or the config.json directly inside Objects/ is reported in the log and ignored.

docs.title: Subfolders
docs.text:
You may sort your files into subfolders of Objects/ as you like, but subfolder names mean nothing: a file is known by its name alone. Objects/Chair/model.fbx is a model for an object called model, not for the chair. Name it Objects/Chair/Chair.fbx instead.

Because Objects/ and all its subfolders count as one pool, two files with the same name in different subfolders clash: the game keeps one and reports the other. Shortcuts (symbolic links and junctions) are never followed.

docs.title: Building the model
docs.text:
• Size and facing. Build the model at the game's scale, in metres, facing the same way as the game's own object. Your model is placed at the original object's origin and is not scaled to fit, so put its origin where the original has it, usually on the ground at the object's centre. An FBX is converted to Y-up and metres on import, and an FBX exported from Blender the usual way faces the same direction as the game's own art.
  • Only the look changes. The object's footprint on the grid, where crew stand to use it and what it bumps into all stay the game's. A model much larger than the original pokes through walls and neighbours.
  • Effects of the original object, such as a workbench's sawdust, keep playing on your model.
  • Static models only. Animation in an FBX is not imported, and the game never animates a mod model.
  • At most 32 MB per model file. A larger file is skipped with a warning, and the object keeps its built-in look.

docs.title: What an FBX may contain
docs.text:
The game reads FBX files itself, so it understands less of the format than Blender can write:

  • Meshes and the hierarchy above them, with position, rotation and scale. Hidden objects are left out, and a file without any mesh is ignored.
  • Normals as exported. A mesh exported without normals gets smooth normals.
  • Only the first UV map. Every further UV map is ignored, so put the UVs your textures use on the first one.
  • Faces with more than three corners are split into triangles. That is only exact for flat, convex faces. Triangulate unusual faces before exporting, or tick Triangulate Faces in Blender's FBX export.
  • Per material: the base colour only. Textures connected to the material, vertex colours and all other material settings are not read.
  • Images embedded in the FBX are never read. Ship the textures as PNG files in Objects/ (see Textures).

docs.title: Textures
docs.text:
Textures are PNG files anywhere in Objects/, found by their names. There are three ways to name them. The game tries them in this order, and each one only fills what the one before left empty:

Name the PNG after Example Needs a model 1 the material in your model: <material>_BaseMap_<UDIM-Tile> and <material>_Specular_<UDIM-Tile> MyChair_BaseMap_1001.png for a material called MyChair yes 2 the texture your model's material uses wood-01.png for a material painted with an image called wood-01 yes 3 a built-in texture of the game BedMetal_Toon-Main_BaseMap_1001.png no

Way 1 is the simplest for a model: you do not have to connect any image to the material in your 3D program. Just give the material and the PNG matching names. Ways 1 and 3 only work with the game's material, which is the default (see Game material or your own).

docs.title: The texture a model names
docs.text:
A model's materials name the images they use, and the game looks for a PNG of that name anywhere in Objects/. A material that uses an image called wood-01 gets Objects/wood-01.png (or Objects/any/subfolder/wood-01.png). Folders and the file extension in the stored name are ignored, so a material painted with C:\art\wood-01.jpg still finds wood-01.png. One PNG can serve any number of models and is loaded only once.

The two model formats differ when no matching PNG is there:

.glb .fbx Texture slots read base colour base colour No PNG of that name in Objects/ the image embedded in the .glb is used the slot stays untextured, and the log names the texture it looked for Images outside the file refused: a .glb has to be self-contained never read: only the PNGs in Objects/ count

Every PNG in Objects/ whose name does not end in .thumbnail counts as a texture. A texture that no model and no built-in object uses is simply never loaded.

docs.title: Re-painting without a model
docs.text:
A PNG named exactly like one of the game's own textures replaces that texture, no model needed. Objects/BedMetal_Toon-Main_BaseMap_1001.png re-paints the metal bed wherever it appears, including its destroyed look. Every object that uses the same texture changes with it.

  • Paint over the original image at the same size and layout, because the model stays the game's own.
  • The game's texture names usually look like <Material>_Toon-Main_BaseMap_<UDIM-Tile> and <Material>_Toon-Main_Specular_<UDIM-Tile>. Every object's texture names are listed on Built-in texture names.
  • Only the object's own art is re-painted. Things every object shares, such as the construction crate, placement markers and range indicators, keep their look. Airplanes (see Airplane skins) and the ground (see Biomes) are not changed this way.
  • If two mods ship the same texture name, the one later in the load order wins.

docs.title: UDIM tiles and specular maps
docs.text:
A model on the game's material can spread its UVs over up to three texture tiles (called UDIM tiles), the way the game's own art does, with a specular map (how shiny each spot is) per tile. For a material called Crate:

Base colour Specular Used for UVs with U in Crate_BaseMap_1001.png Crate_Specular_1001.png 0 to 1 Crate_BaseMap_1002.png Crate_Specular_1002.png 1 to 2 Crate_BaseMap_1003.png Crate_Specular_1003.png 2 and above
  • Names after the material (way 1) are tried first, for the base colour and for each specular map on its own. A mod may ship only Crate_Specular_1001.png.
  • If no base colour is named after the material, the texture your model uses (way 2) becomes tile 1001, and the other tiles and specular maps are named after it. The tile number follows a _ or a .: crate_1001 and crate.1001 both start a set, and a Blender tile set saved as crate.<UDIM>.png finds crate.1001.png. The specular map has the same name with _BaseMap replaced by _Specular, so it only works when the texture name contains _BaseMap.
  • Tiles switch on when the 1001 base colour has at least one more tile. A single texture is drawn as usual. A missing tile in between is drawn white.
  • A specular map or base colour your mod does not ship leaves the original object's own one in place.
  • A base colour named after the material is drawn as it is: the colour the material has in your model is ignored, because an FBX material without an image still carries Blender's grey default.

docs.title: Game material or your own
docs.text:
By default your model is drawn with the game's own material for that object, using your model's base colour texture and base colour. That is what makes battle damage and the other effects the game paints onto objects show on your model too. Specular maps and UDIM tiles are used too.

To keep the material exactly as you made it instead, switch the game's material off for that object in Objects/config.json. Only the config.json directly inside Objects/ is read:

{
  "Objects": {
    "Chair": { "UseGameMaterial": false }
  }
}
  • The keys are object ids as in the file names, without regard to capitals.
  • An object with "UseGameMaterial": false keeps its full look from your 3D program, but does not show battle damage. It also only uses the texture its material names (way 2), without specular maps or UDIM tiles.
  • Even with false, a material without a base colour texture uses the game's material anyway, keeping the colour you gave it.
  • A config.json the game cannot read is reported in the log, and every object falls back to the default.

docs.title: Thumbnails
docs.text:
<objectId>.thumbnail.png replaces the object's icon in the build menu and everywhere else that icon is shown.

  • At most 512 × 512 pixels, and at most 10 MB. Each side counts on its own, so 512 × 256 is fine. A larger thumbnail is not scaled down: it is skipped with a warning in the log, and the game's own icon stays.
  • A thumbnail is only used next to a model with the same id. It cannot change the icon of an object your mod does not give a new model; a thumbnail on its own is reported and ignored.
  • One thumbnail per object. A second file with the same name in another subfolder is ignored.

docs.title: File limits
docs.text:
Every file in Objects/ and Biomes/ is checked before it is loaded:

File Largest picture Largest file Model (.glb, .fbx) - 32 MB Texture 4096 × 4096 10 MB Thumbnail 512 × 512 10 MB Biome 4096 × 4096 10 MB
  • Every image has to be a real PNG. A JPEG renamed to .png is refused.
  • The picture limit applies to each side on its own.
  • An image over its limit is never scaled down. It is skipped with a warning in the log, and the game falls back: a skipped thumbnail leaves the game's own icon, a skipped biome the game's own ground, and a material whose texture was skipped is drawn without it.

docs.title: Several mods changing the same object
docs.text: If two enabled mods change the same object, the mod applied last wins, following the load order (see How mods work). The log says which mod overrode which. An object is decided as a whole: one mod's model is never combined with another mod's thumbnail for the same object.

docs.title: When something does not show up
docs.text:
• Did you restart the game? Art is only imported at game start.
  • Is the mod switched on in Main menu -> Mods?
  • Does the file name match an id exactly (apart from capitals)? Is the subfolder name doing nothing you rely on?
  • Is every file within the limits above, and every image a real PNG?
  • For an FBX: are the textures shipped as PNGs in Objects/, named after the material or the image the material uses?

The game writes what it refused and why (a wrong name, a missing texture, an image that is too big) to Player.log, on lines that start with [Mod <your mod id>]. The detailed lines may only appear in development builds, so if the log is silent, check the list above and look at the object in the game.

docs.title: Built-in texture names
docs.text:
A PNG in your mod's Objects/ folder that is named exactly like one of the game's own textures replaces that texture on every object that uses it. You do not need a model for this: the game keeps its own model and paints your picture onto it. Objects/BedMetal_Toon-Main_BaseMap_1001.png, for example, re-paints the metal bed. The rules are on Objects and models.

Some textures are shared by several objects. Such a texture is listed under each of them, and replacing it changes all of them at once. Paint your replacement at the same size and layout as the original, because the model stays the game's own.

The Slot column says what the texture does on the object:

Slot What it holds _BaseMap the base colour; for objects with several tiles, tile 1001 (UVs with U from 0 to 1) _BaseMap1002, _BaseMap1003 the base colour of tiles 1002 (U from 1 to 2) and 1003 (U from 2) _SpecularMap the specular colour, how shiny each spot is; for objects with several tiles, tile 1001 _SpecularMap1002, _SpecularMap1003 the specular colour of tiles 1002 and 1003

The slot is only information: your file is named after the texture, never after the slot. Other slots the game uses internally (for example for battle damage, snow or fading out) are left out of these tables.

These tables were taken from the game's generated texture list on 2026-10-01.

docs.title: CSV tables
docs.text:
Most of the numbers that drive Ground of Aces - what a building costs, how fast a plane flies, how much a meal lifts a crew member's mood - live in data tables. A mod can change any of them without touching the game's code, by dropping a small file into its own folder.

This page is the complete reference: where the files go, what the two file formats look like, what the game checks before it accepts a value, and what every table and column means. Every table section in The tables starts with a link to the built-in file, so you can open the real thing or save it and copy its header row.

Note

Nothing here can permanently damage your game. A value the game cannot use is refused and written to the log with the reason; the built-in value stays. Removing the mod folder restores everything.

Tip

The single-cell <Table>.json command files are covered step by step, with more examples, on Table command files.

One mod is one folder in your Mods folder, and the data tables go into its CSV/ subfolder:

Mods/
  my_balance_mod/
    config.json
    CSV/
      VehicleData.csv    whole rows
      Variables.json     single cells

Where the Mods folder is, what config.json may contain and how several mods are ordered is explained once, on How mods work. The folder itself can have any name. The one rule that matters here: if you give the mod an Id in config.json, it must be 3–64 characters of lower-case letters, digits, _, . or -, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is ignored without a message and the lower-cased folder name is used instead.

Only files directly inside CSV/ are read - subfolders are ignored.

docs.title: Your first mod
docs.text:
Make the wooden wall cost one plank instead of two. Create Mods/my_balance_mod/CSV/ResourceCost.json containing:

{
  "Commands": [
    { "Command": "Replace", "Id": "wall_wood", "Cells": { "Planks": 1 } }
  ]
}

Start the game, load a level, and the wall costs one plank. That is the whole mod - no manifest, no registration.

docs.title: The two file formats
docs.text:
A file is named after the table it changes, matched exactly, capital letters included: VehicleData.csv, never vehicledata.csv. A file naming a table that does not exist is skipped, and the log says so.

You may use either format, or both. Within one mod the .csv files are applied first and the .json files after, so a command can refine a row a CSV file added.

docs.title: Single cells - <Table>.json
docs.text:
A list of commands, run top to bottom. This is the format to reach for: it touches only the values you name and leaves everything else alone.

{
  "Commands": [
    { "Command": "Replace", "Id": "gladiator", "Cells": { "Fuel Capacity": 350, "Movement Speed": 7 } },
    { "Command": "Add",     "Id": "storage_box", "Cells": { "Planks": 3, "Metal": 1 } },
    { "Command": "Remove",  "Id": "Chair", "Columns": [ "Tarp" ] },
    { "Command": "Remove",  "Id": "Drawer" }
  ]
}
Command Fields What it does Replace Id, Cells Changes only the listed cells of an existing row. Everything else keeps its value. Add Id, Cells Adds a new row. Only possible in ResourceCost and PropsInfluence (see Adding and removing rows). Remove with Columns Id, Columns Clears the listed cells of a row. Remove without Columns Id Removes the whole row. Only in ResourceCost and PropsInfluence.

Rules of the format:

  • Plain JSON - no comments, no trailing commas.
  • Command and Id ignore capitalisation. The keys inside Cells and the entries in Columns are column headers and must match exactly, including spaces.
  • Values may be written as JSON strings, numbers or booleans - 300, 1.5, true and "300" all work.
  • An empty string, a string of only spaces, or null in Cells clears that cell, the same as listing it under Columns in a Remove.
  • Remove does not take Cells; list the cells to clear in Columns.
  • At most 200 commands per file. A file that does not parse, or has no Commands, is skipped whole.
  • Each command is judged on its own - a bad one is skipped with a warning and the rest still apply.

docs.title: Whole rows - <Table>.csv
docs.text:
A spreadsheet file carrying complete rows. Use this when you would rather edit a table in a spreadsheet program and ship the finished rows.

Name,Value
TurboTimeScaleMultiplier,20
RandomActionChatProbability,0.6
  • The header row must list exactly the table's columns: the id column first, then every value column, in any order, none missing and none extra. The id column's own header is ignored, so only the value columns have to match.
  • Include only the rows you want to change - a file does not have to cover the whole table.
  • A row whose id matches a built-in row replaces that row completely. Ids ignore capitalisation.
  • Give every row the same number of cells as the header row. A short row makes the file unreadable and the whole file is skipped; extra cells beyond the header are silently ignored.
  • A cell that contains a comma must be quoted, as a spreadsheet program does: "Sleep,Chill". A line break inside a quoted cell is not supported - it ends the row.
  • At most 200 rows per file. Fully blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored, so you can leave notes. A line that starts with an empty id cell but has other cells is read as a continuation of the row above, and that row is then refused as spanning several lines.
  • The same id on two separate lines makes the file unreadable; on two neighbouring lines it is treated as one row and refused.
  • Each row is judged on its own - a bad row is skipped and the built-in row stays.

docs.title: Columns only take the kind of value they already hold
docs.text: A column that holds numbers in every built-in row takes only numbers; one that holds TRUE/FALSE takes only those. Movement Speed = fast is refused. Columns that hold text are freer, but most of them still have a rule of their own - the tables further down say which values each one accepts.

docs.title: Empty cells
docs.text:
A cell may only be left empty in a column where the game already leaves some row empty. Everywhere else, blanking a cell is refused, because the game has no "no value" case for it.

Two columns are special and are filled in for you instead of being left blank:

  • Any ResourceCost cell you leave out, clear, or set to "" becomes 0. An Add therefore only needs the resources that actually cost something.
  • Associated Task in BuildingComponents becomes None, meaning "this object gives no task".

docs.title: Adding and removing rows
docs.text:
You are normally changing cells of rows that already exist. Whole rows can only be added or removed in two tables, because everywhere else the game and your save files expect a fixed set of ids:

Table Rows can be added or removed ResourceCost yes, for any built-in object or aircraft id PropsInfluence yes, for any built-in object or aircraft id every other table no

An added row must use an id that already exists as a building object or an aircraft - you are giving an existing thing a build cost or a mood effect it did not have, not inventing a new thing.

docs.title: Rows that take up several lines
docs.text:
A few tables spread one row over several lines, because that row holds a list - a task with several settings, a mood effect with one variant per bed type. A single mod row cannot express a list, so those rows are refused. The table sections below name them.

In ResourceCost only, some rows carry a leftover heading in their Money cell and so count as several lines. There a whole-row CSV is the fix: it rewrites every cell and tidies the row up at the same time. The affected ids are KickstarterCustomMonument, RadioTower, window_wood, window_tent, window_brick, window_hangar, window_concrete, Distillery, ParkingLarge and gravel.

docs.title: Checking what happened
docs.text:
Every accepted change and every refusal is one line in the game's log, Player.log. On Windows there is also an HTML version in the same folder that is easier to read. The label at the start of each line is the mod's id.

[Mod my_balance_mod] CSV/ResourceCost.json command 1 replaced cells Planks of row 'wall_wood'.
[Mod my_balance_mod] CSV/VehicleData.csv overrides built-in row 'gladiator'.
[Mod my_balance_mod] CSV/PropsInfluence.json command 4 removed row 'Drawer'.

A refusal names the file, the row or command number, and the reason:

[Mod my_balance_mod] CSV/VehicleData.json command 3 rejected: 'Fight Power' exceeds 2x the highest built-in value (60).
[Mod my_balance_mod] CSV/AirBaseData.json command 1 rejected: 'Missions Per Week' holds numbers in every built-in row; 'seven' is not one.

Note

These lines are written as information and warnings. The released game logs errors only, so you will see them only in a development build or in the Unity editor. In the released game, check the effect in the game instead - load a level and look at the value you changed.

A misspelled table name or a header row that does not match still produces a skipped: line naming the file. If you see no [Mod ...] lines at all and the change does not show, the game did not pick the mod up: the CSV/ folder was still empty when the game started (press Refresh in the Mods window), the mod is switched off in the Mods window, or the mod folder is a symbolic link or junction, which is never followed.

docs.title: Finding a table's column headers
docs.text: The game ships header templates for four tables (BuildingComponents, PropsInfluence, ResourceCost and VehicleData) in Ground Of Aces_Data/StreamingAssets/Modding/Templates/ inside the installation folder (on macOS: Ground of Aces.app/Contents/Resources/Data/StreamingAssets/Modding/Templates/). For the rest, the column list is on this page, and every table section links the built-in file. Or ask the game: write a deliberately wrong header, load once, and the log prints the columns it expected.

docs.title: Load order
docs.text: Mods are applied in the order described on Which mod wins - Workshop first, then your own, lower LoadOrder first. When two mods change the same row, the later one wins for the cells it touches: a whole-row CSV replaces everything an earlier mod did to that row, a Replace only the cells it names. A mod switched off in the Mods window contributes nothing.

docs.title: When changes take effect
docs.text:
CSV tables are rebuilt every time a level is loaded - return to the main menu and load again. The same happens when the main menu or the map editor opens. Edit a file while a level is running and the change appears on the next load, so you can try out values without restarting. A file you keep open in a spreadsheet program is still read.

A brand-new mod folder, a CSV/ folder that was still empty when the game started, or a changed config.json needs the game to look at the mod list again: press Refresh in the Mods window (main menu → Mods) and then load a level, or restart the game.

docs.title: The tables
docs.text:
Thirty tables can be modded. Three files that exist in the game but are not loaded - ResourceDegradation, StartTimeValues and StateInfluence - cannot.

Each section lists the columns, what values they take, and what the built-in rows use. Where a column has no special rule, only the generic ones above apply.

The built-in values are always complete, never a sample:

  • a–b is the full range: the lowest and the highest value any built-in row uses.
  • A list joined by "or" is every distinct value the built-in rows use.
  • A list marked "by row" gives each row's value, in the order the rows appear in the file.
  • "on every row" means all built-in rows hold that one value.
  • A min-max column gives each half its own range: "min 0–43, max 0–60" means the first number runs from 0 to 43 across the rows and the second from 0 to 60.
  • An empty built-in cell means the built-in rows use every value listed under Value.

docs.title: VehicleData - aircraft
docs.text:
Built-in file: VehicleData.csv

One row per aircraft. Rows cannot be added or removed.

Column Value Built-in Notes Name localization key airplane/<row id> on every row, e.g. airplane/spitfire must not be empty Type Fighter, Bomber, MultiRole, Special Crew comma list of seats; repeat a role for two seats 1–8 seats, from Pilot alone to Pilot,Pilot,BombAimer,Navigator,FlightEngineer,RadioOperator,Gunner,Gunner; every row starts with Pilot and all six roles are used in a CSV file, wrap a cell with more than one seat in quotes: "Pilot,Gunner,Navigator". Roles: Pilot, Gunner, Navigator, BombAimer, FlightEngineer, RadioOperator Runway Tier whole number 1–5 above 5 and no airstrip can serve it Parking Size parking spot size: 0 small, 1 medium, 2 large 0–2 above 2 and it can never park Victory Points Cost whole number 0–12 0 makes it free Movement Speed whole number 5 on every row taxi speed; 0 and it never reaches the runway Landing Length whole number 60–170 longer than the strip and the plane overshoots it on landing Health whole number 100 on every row Initial Integrity whole number 1000 on every row hours of wear the aircraft can take before it is worn out (1000 h ≈ 41 days) Fuel Capacity whole number 200–1260 Voxel Size AxBxC 10x0x10 on every row Fight Power min-max min 0–43, max 0–60 0 ≤ min ≤ max Bomb Power min-max min 0–50, max 0–80 0 ≤ min ≤ max Recon Power min-max min 5–42, max 10–60 0 ≤ min ≤ max Manoeuvrability min-max min 2–28, max 8–50 0 ≤ min ≤ max Transport Capacity min-max min 1–60, max 5–90 0 ≤ min ≤ max Stealthiness min-max min 10–88, max 48–98 0 ≤ min ≤ max; hard cap: max at most 100, a higher value breaks the game. At 100 the plane is invisible to the enemy. Wreck Resource Type /-list of resources Metal/RepairParts on every row both wreck columns set, or both empty Wreck Resource Amount /-list of whole numbers 10/5 on every row one amount per entry in Wreck Resource Type, in the order listed there Low Caliber Ammo Capacity whole number 0–3300 GunAmmo carried; 0 = none High Caliber Ammo Capacity whole number 0–300 AntiAirAmmo carried; 0 = none Plane Bombs Capacity whole number 0–32 PlaneBombs carried; 0 = none

Warning

An aircraft already parked at your base keeps the health, integrity and fuel capacity it was built with. Only newly delivered aircraft pick up changed values - so a save made while a mod was active keeps that mod's numbers even after you remove it.

docs.title: AirBaseData - the HQ rank ladder
docs.text:
Built-in file: AirBaseData.csv

Rows 1–6, one per base category. All six must exist and their ids cannot change.

Column Value Built-in Notes Airstrip Tier whole number by row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5 required to reach the rank Minimum Airstrip Count whole number 1–5 Minimum Parking Count whole number 1–20 Missions Per Week whole number 6–18 slots the week offers; 0 and no missions are scheduled Minimum Missions Per Week whole number 2–10 the weekly HQ quota: how many missions the base must fly to a result each week. Won and lost missions count; cancelled ones and failed historic missions do not. Missing this or Minimum Success Rate halves the next shipment's slots (rounded up) and, on the normal HQ strikes setting, adds a strike - three weeks missed in a row end the run. Training weeks and the "no requirements" HQ setting skip the check. Above Missions Per Week makes the quota impossible Minimum Success Rate fraction, not percent 0.4–0.8 share of the missions counted by Minimum Missions Per Week that must be won; above 1 is unachievable Available Shipment Slots whole number 4–8 0 disables supply

docs.title: AirstripTiers
docs.text:
Built-in file: AirstripTiers.csv

Rows 1–5.

Column Value Built-in Notes Length whole number by row: 80, 120, 140, 160, 200 tiers match on "length or more", so keep them ascending Width whole number by row: 12, 14, 18, 22, 26 tiers match on "width or more", so keep them ascending Material text by row: dirt, sand, gravel, concrete, tarmac must name an existing ResourceCost row - that row is what each tile of this runway costs. ResourceCost does not accept new surface rows, so in practice keep to dirt, sand, gravel, concrete and tarmac (swapping them between tiers is fine). A material with no ResourceCost row is accepted here, and then laying a runway of that tier fails with an error Biome Id whole number by row: 6, 20, 22, 15, 13 ground painted under the finished strip Build Time whole number by row: 5, 2, 2, 2, 2 in-game minutes of work per tile. Each tile is worked by one crew member at a time, so more crew lay more tiles in parallel, not one tile faster

docs.title: Biomes
docs.text:
Built-in file: Biomes.csv

Rows 0–23, the ground types. All columns are numbers, so this table is easy to tune safely.

Column Built-in Notes Airstrip Tier 0–5 tier a runway laid on this ground counts as Character Speed Modifier 1–1.2 0 freezes anyone standing on it Airplane Speed Modifier 0.5–1.2 Degradation Penalty 0–0.2 extra wear on goods stored here Fire Spread Modifier 0.5 or 1

docs.title: AttacksComposition - what an air raid is made of
docs.text:
Built-in file: AttacksComposition.csv

The row id is the raid severity. Normal play reaches 1–25; rows 99, 101, 200 and 300 are not reached by the normal severity ladder and are kept for special raids. The ranges below describe rows 1–25. The four special rows point at themselves in the last two columns and hold:

Row Bombers Divers Fighters 99 9-9 6-6 8-8 200 10-10 0-0 0-0 300 0-0 10-10 0-0 101 0-0 3-3 2-2 Column Value Built-in (rows 1–25) Notes Bombers min-max min 0–4, max 0–6 whole numbers, 0 ≤ min ≤ max Divers min-max min 0–6, max 0–6 whole numbers, 0 ≤ min ≤ max Fighters min-max min 1–8, max 2–8 whole numbers, 0 ≤ min ≤ max LowAttacks whole number 1–14 severity used instead when the map is set to easier raids - must name a row this table has HighAttacks whole number 2–25 severity used when the map is set to harder raids - must name a row this table has

docs.title: EquipmentData - AA guns, searchlights, towers
docs.text:
Built-in file: EquipmentData.csv

Rows are equipment ids: Bofors40mm, Searchlight, RadioTower, VickersGunAA, OerlikonGun, Lookout, ControlTowerMetal, ControlTowerBrick, ControlTowerConcrete.

Column Value Built-in Notes Range number 10–70 0 makes the piece useless Damage number 0–6 0 makes the piece a non-firing station like the Searchlight or Lookout: it can still be placed and crewed, but it never shoots, and every column from Fire Rate onward is not read for it Fire Rate whole number 0–720 rounds per minute Ammo Type resource name or None GunAmmo, AntiAirAmmo, None or 0 anything that is not a resource name (None, 0) means the piece stores no ammo Ammo Capacity whole number 0–80 rounds loaded at once Ammo Load Time number 0–6.5 seconds to reload Ammo Storage whole number 0–500 0 means it never draws ammo Damage Bonus number 0 or 0.25 granted to others in range (searchlight) Firing Angle number 0, 140 or 360 0 is read as a full circle Aiming Speed number 0–170 degrees per second Range Bonus number 0 or 16 granted to others in range (lookout) Attacker Priority Bombers, Divers, Fighters, Nearest, None Bombers, Divers, Fighters or None; no row uses Nearest anything else falls back to None

docs.title: BuildingComponents - objects and building parts
docs.text:
Built-in file: BuildingComponents.csv

One row per object, wall piece, floor, roof, workbench and piece of equipment. Rows cannot be added or removed.

Column Value Built-in Notes Dimensions WxHxD, or dynamic/1x0x1 for roofs width 1–32, height 0–6, depth 1–32 (from 1x0x1 to 32x1x32), dynamic/1x0x1 on the roofs, empty on 9 rows (listed below) Build Time whole number 0–420 in-game minutes of work. One crew member builds an object at a time; extra crew do not speed it up Health whole number 0–10000 the huge value marks the indestructible pieces Associated Task task name or None None, Sleep, Chill, UseEquipment, PlayPiano, UseTrainingObject, MonitorAirspace, UseRadio, SaluteTheFlag, Grieve, ListenToMusic, PlayDartboard, PlayGuitar, PlayBilliardTable or UsePlanningBoard pointing an object at a task its art does not fit is allowed, and looks wrong Users Limit whole number 0–5 0 on a usable object means nobody can use it Is Wall Deco TRUE/FALSE Is Floor Deco TRUE/FALSE Is Fireproof TRUE/FALSE Placement Requirement None, Indoors, Outdoors

Note

A Replace is checked against the finished row, so a row that leaves Dimensions or Users Limit empty cannot be patched unless you also set that cell in the same command - or ship the row as CSV. Empty Dimensions: PropagandaPoster, MusicPoster, AirplanePoster, CompanyMascotPoster, CurtainsClosed, CurtainsOpen, EntranceSign, tombstone, storage_box. Empty Users Limit: the workbenches and the three parking sizes.

docs.title: ResourceCost - what something costs to build
docs.text:
Built-in file: ResourceCost.csv

One row per object or aircraft id, one column per resource. Rows can be added and removed. A removed row means "no build cost". A cost of 0 means "not required", so zeroing every column has the same effect. An added row's id must be an existing BuildingComponents or VehicleData id; anything else is refused as "neither a built-in prop nor a built-in plane".

Every cell is a whole number, zero or more. The columns are:

Money  VictoryPoints  Trash  Wood  Clay  Sandbags  Stone  Food  RawWater  Herbs  Metal  Bricks
Planks  Tarp  Cement  Fuel  PurifiedWater  Meals  SimpleMedicine  Intel  Machinery  Electronics
LuxuryGoods  MilitaryConstruction  Camouflage  FoodRations  StrongMedicine  RepairParts  GunAmmo
AntiAirAmmo  PlaneBombs

Runway surfaces are rows here too - dirt, sand, gravel, concrete, tarmac - so changing gravel changes what a tier-3 runway costs per tile. Do not remove a surface row: unlike an object, a surface with no row does not become free - laying a runway of that tier fails with an error. To make a surface free, set every cell of its row to 0.

docs.title: PropsInfluence - the mood effect an object radiates
docs.text:
Built-in file: PropsInfluence.csv

One row per object that lifts or lowers the mood of crew nearby. Rows can be added and removed; an object without a row simply has no effect.

Column Value Built-in Notes Buff Name localization key a prop_effects/<effect> key on every row (31 different keys), e.g. prop_effects/organised_sleep must not be empty Radius number 0.5–50 in tiles; the control towers reach 20, 30 and 50 Associated Tasks Or Action comma list of task names 1–4 names per row, e.g. Sleep or "Sleep,Chill", drawn from AidInjured, BoardAirplane, BringResources, Bury, Chill, Cook, Eat, Grieve, HarvestGardeningTile, Landing, Loiter, MaintainAirplane, PlayGuitar, PlayPiano, Recover, RecoverInBed, Repair, RepairAirplane, Sleep, Stockpile, UseEquipment, UsePlanningBoard, UseRadio, UseTrainingObject, Water or WorkOnWorkbench must not be empty. In a CSV file, wrap a cell with more than one task in quotes: "Sleep,Chill". A name that matches no task is accepted and the effect simply never fires Effect 1 <signed number> <name> -1 Mood to +3 Mood, +1 Energy to +2 Energy, +0.5 Confidence to +10 Confidence, or -1 Accident names: Mood, Confidence, Energy Effect 2 <signed number> <name>, or empty -1.5 Energy, +1 Energy, +0.5 Mood, +10 Mood or +1 Confidence on 9 rows; empty on the rest Effect 3 <signed number> <name>, or empty empty on every row

The sign is part of the number, so 1 Mood means +1. Names are matched loosely, so +1 mood works. A name other than the three above is stored as a special effect (the game uses -1 Accident on the three control towers); an invented name is accepted and does nothing.

docs.title: MapObjects - trees, rocks, ponds and other harvestables
docs.text:
Built-in file: MapObjects.csv

One row per world object. Ids are used by map files and cannot change.

Column Value Built-in Notes LocKey_Name localization key map.obj.<object>.name on 20 rows, e.g. map.obj.tree.name; map.obj.<object> without .name on the other 13, e.g. map.obj.crate LocKey_Description localization key map.obj.<object>.description on 18 rows, e.g. map.obj.tree.description; map.obj.<object> without .description on the other 15, e.g. map.obj.crate Dimensions WxHxD width 1–4, height 1–6, depth 1–6 (from 1x1x1 to 4x6x4) Resource Harvested resource name, or empty Wood, Stone, Herbs, Food, RawWater, Clay, Sandbags, Metal, Planks, Fuel, GrainSeeds, BeansSeeds, PotatoSeeds or TomatoSeeds; empty on 9 rows empty means nothing to harvest Farming Time whole number 0–400 in-game minutes of work per harvest, by one crew member at a time Resource Amount whole number 0–50 yield per harvest Resource Total whole number 0–500 total before it is used up Limited Harvest Amount whole number 0, 20, 30 or 100 cap for endless sources; 0 = uncapped Destroyed On Depletion TRUE/FALSE FALSE with Refresh Time 0 leaves something that can never be harvested again Refresh Time whole number 0–21600 minutes until it regrows Health whole number 1–2147483647 the huge value marks the indestructible ones Is Fireproof TRUE/FALSE TRUE on the rocks, pits, pond, ocean, WaterPump and WaterTower TRUE makes the object a firebreak: fire can neither start on nor spread onto the tiles it covers. Fire still crosses the open ground around it

Two rows, young_tree and young_tree_big.
